calls.reason: RBC reports stretched valuations but also stronger fundamentals than during the dot-com bubble. Its analysis does not establish whether AI investment broadly exceeded plausible returns.

Revenera finds provider margin pressure, while Nvidia reports strong revenue growth. Neither establishes broad customer and provider profit failure or the resulting order response; the canary prediction is also hedged.

Pew documents widespread daily chatbot use and different search behavior, and OpenAI reports 700 million weekly users. These challenge the claim but do not clearly settle the undefined iPhone comparison.

Epoch projects a possible data constraint but finds mixed synthetic-data results. Phi-2 and Gerstgrasser's experiments show useful approaches without settling whether they resolve the industry-wide shortage.

Schneider documents cooling challenges and feasible remedies; CBRE reports power constraints on data-center locations. Neither establishes that these obstacles substantially limit further AI progress.
XPS and FT reporting support the first-quarter ranking and AI's contribution. The central concern about an unstable hype cycle is explicitly a fear, which those market reports do not settle.
